title: Lexicon corrections, public copy (open-greek-lexica 0.3.0)
description: corrections.json: reversible changes to the source, applied in order before conversion. inverse is the same change with original and correction exchanged. The public copy in a lexicon's repository leaves out these fields of each record: evidence.

error_in.description: Where the error is: in the printed book (a correction of the author) or in the source encoding (the print is right).

target.description: What the record changes. element: entry (xml:id), element (name), occurrences, and optionally nth (position among the elements of that name in the entry, counted after earlier records). page-break: entry, anchor. move: div, entry or entry_of. insert-element: entry, element, nth (insert before that element; with after: true, right after it). remove-element: div (a top-level element), or entry, element, nth (an element inside an entry). insert-entry: div (the xml:id of the entry). text: page, col, line, offset. start: page, col, line.

after.description: insert-element only: insert right after the nth element and its text instead of before it.

correction.description: The changed state. element: {attributes, text} (an attribute the original names and the correction does not is removed), and tail (the exact text after the element) when the original gives one, or xml (the exact XML of the element, whose content is replaced) where the change adds or drops a child (a record on a paragraph, p, changes only its text); page-break: {pb}; move: {parent, index}; insert-element: {xml, tail}; remove-element: {index, xml, tail} (top-level) or {xml, tail} (inside an entry), or null; insert-entry: {index, xml, tail}, the entry the source lost, typed from the scan, at that position among the children of the body; text: {text}; start: {start}, whether the line begins an entry.

summary.description: One line for readers: what was wrong and what the print or the evidence shows. Copied into the correction mark.

print_reading.description: The reading of the print, when it differs from both the original and the correction (the print and the source are wrong in different ways). Copied into the correction mark.

scan.description: Where the evidence can be seen: {vol, page, col}.
